from typing import List, Set, Any

def power_set(nums: List[Any]) -> List[List[Any]]:
    """
    Computes the power set of a given list.

    The power set is the set of all possible subsets of the input set.

    Args:
        nums: The input list of elements.

    Returns:
        A list of lists, where each inner list is a subset of the input list.
    """
    n = len(nums)
    # The power set will have 2^n subsets.
    # We can represent each subset using a bitmask from 0 to 2^n - 1.
    power_set_list: List[List[Any]] = []

    # Iterate through all numbers from 0 to 2^n - 1
    for i in range(1 << n):  # 1 << n is equivalent to 2**n
        subset: List[Any] = []
        # Check each element of the input list
        for j in range(n):
            # If the j-th bit of 'i' is set (i.e., equal to 1), 
            # include the j-th element of nums in the current subset.
            if (i >> j) & 1:
                subset.append(nums[j])
        power_set_list.append(subset)

    return power_set_list

This is a very efficient and common way to generate all subsets. Each number from $0$ to $2^n - 1$ can be used as a bitmask to represent a unique subset. If the $j$-th bit of the number is set, it means the $j$-th element of the original list is included in that subset.
